findings.title: [P1] Do not render cancellation of superseded searches as an error
findings.body: Every call to `search` starts by aborting the previous controller (`this.active?.abort()`), so a second search while one is in flight causes the first request's promise to reject with an abort error (any `api.search` honoring the signal, e.g. fetch-backed, behaves this way). The new unconditional `catch` at `src/search.ts:26-27` then calls `this.renderError(error)` for that ordinary cancellation, so rapid successive searches — the exact scenario the abort pattern exists to support — display a spurious error from an obsolete query, potentially clobbering newer UI state. The catch should distinguish abort/cancellation of superseded requests (ignore them, or at least not render them as errors) from genuine failures of the current request.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the search method's rejection contract
findings.body: Before this change, failures of `api.search` and exceptions from `render` rejected the promise returned by `search`, so callers could observe failures via `await`/`.catch`. The new `catch` at `src/search.ts:23-27` consumes both and, when `renderError` returns normally, makes `search` resolve with `undefined` — failures become unobservable to awaiters. This contradicts the PR's stated intent of "preserving existing contracts." Render the error and then rethrow (or otherwise retain the prior rejection semantics), e.g. `catch (error) { this.renderError(error); throw error; }`.
